findings.title: Preserve the original 30% lightness for metadata links
findings.body: This was previously `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the new primary branch uses 70% and the secondary branch uses 30%. The conversion should preserve 30% for `$primary` and use 70% for `$secondary`. As written, these author links become substantially lighter in the regular theme and use the wrong shade in dark themes.

findings.title: Preserve the original 30% lightness for group member names
findings.body: The group member name color was previously scaled from `$primary` by 30%, but this change uses 50% for both theme branches. It should retain 30% for `$primary` and use 70% for `$secondary`; the current value changes the name color in the regular theme and produces the wrong shade in dark themes.

findings.title: Do not reverse the custom-message length color lightness
findings.body: This was previously `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the new primary branch uses 30% and the secondary branch uses 70%. The conversion should preserve 70% for `$primary` and use 30% for `$secondary`. This makes the text unexpectedly darker in the regular theme and gives it the wrong shade in dark themes.

findings.title: Preserve the original 20% lightness for topic-map headings
findings.body: This heading was previously scaled from `$primary` by 20%, but the new value uses 50% for both theme branches. It should retain 20% for `$primary` and use 80% for `$secondary`; the current value changes the heading color in the regular theme and uses the wrong shade in dark themes.

findings.title: Preserve the original 30% lightness for group member names
findings.body: The group member name color was previously scaled from `$primary` by 30%, but this change uses 50% for both theme branches. It should retain 30% for `$primary` and use 70% for `$secondary`; the current value changes the name color in the regular theme and produces the wrong shade in dark themes.

findings.title: Apply the dark-theme color choice to category notification badges
findings.body: This category badge text still uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` directly, while the other muted topic-list text colors were updated to choose a `$secondary`-derived value for dark themes. Consequently, category notification counts keep the primary-derived shade in dark themes instead of the intended muted shade.
